chosen.title: Barbell Shrugs: Know The Difference ⚠️ #back
chosen.description:
Know The Difference ⚠️
.
Here are the two main variations of Barbell Shrugs you want to be aware of.

When using a Wide Grip with your Body Upright, this will emphasize your Upper Traps since you’re Upwardly Rotating your Scapula (Shoulders to Ears). ✅

However, when using a Narrow Grip and Leaning your Hips Back, this will shift emphasis to your Mid Traps due to Scapular Retraction (Bringing Shoulder Blades Together). ✅

Save this for next time you do Barbell Shrugs. 🔥

Keep crushing it saiyans 💪🏽
.

candidates.title: ❌ You're Doing Dumbbell Shrugs WRONG!
candidates.description:
❌ You're Doing Dumbbell Shrugs WRONG!

Mistake #1: Hunching Your Back
This puts stress on your spine and increases the risk of injury. Instead, keep a neutral back with your chest tall and core braced.

Mistake #2: Holding the Dumbbells at Your Sides
When the dumbbells are directly beside you, they can rub against your thighs, making the movement awkward and less effective.. Try positioning them slightly in front of your body.

Mistake #3: Staying Fully Upright
Staying completely vertical limits trap engagement. Leaning forward slightly hits more of the upper and middle traps—and often feels more natural on your shoulders.

Mistake #4: Rolling Your Shoulders
Rolling adds unnecessary joint stress and does nothing for muscle activation. Shrug straight up and down with control.

candidates.title: ❌ 1 Barbell Shrug Mistake (FIX THIS)
candidates.description:
If you want to build bigger traps, you need to make sure you're using proper shrugs form during your back workouts. One common barbell shrug mistake is using too wide of a grip. This reduces your ability to build upper traps since it doesn't optimally line the resistance up with those fibers. Instead, when performing this back exercise make sure to use a wider grip a few inches outside of shoulder width. You'll build your upper trapezius more effectively this way.
